_doc: Inflation benchmarks for retrospective editions dated in 2017: the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at each cutoff. End-2016 state of the verified 2016 register (China's ~3% objective of 5 Mar 2016; the RBA's Statement of 19 Sep 2016; the FOMC's 2% goal, the BoJ's 2% target, New Zealand's 2012 PTA, Korea's 2% for the three years from 2016), plus the 2017 current-year targets set earlier: Türkiye 5% (CBRT policy document of 10 Dec 2014, para 1, restated 6 Dec 2016 with the ±2pp band); Brazil 4.5% ±1.5 (CMN Res. 4,419 of 25 Jun 2015); Colombia 3% ±1 (Board of 25 Nov 2016); Indonesia 4% ±1 (PMK 93/PMK.011/2014); Thailand 2.5% ±1.5 (Cabinet, 20 Dec 2016; BoT and FPO announcements of 21 Dec 2016); Canada 2% under the renewal of 24 Oct 2016, now the agreement in force; India 5% (RBI MPC, 4 Oct 2016: 5 per cent by Q4 of the fiscal year ending in March, within the statutory 4% ±2). Changes announced during 2017: China's annual objective (5 Mar 2017: around 3%, value unchanged, recorded for its wording); India 5 → 4 from the MPC resolution of 6 Apr 2017 (the Q4 objective reached its horizon; the 8 Feb 2017 resolution still named the 5 per cent objective); Sweden's switch of the target variable from CPI to CPIF (7 Sep 2017; value unchanged at 2%, recorded because it replaces the row's index and wording). Value-unchanged reaffirmations are not recorded: the FOMC's annual reaffirmation of its statement of longer-run goals, the UK remit of 8 Mar 2017, and New Zealand's unchanged Policy Targets Agreements (dated 6 Jun 2017, in force from 27 Sep 2017; 7 Nov 2017), which keep the 1–3% range with the 2% midpoint focus of the 2012 agreement; Korea's 2% (no 2017 change). Every new source was fetched and its quoted text checked (the Bank of Thailand announcement is a scanned PDF, its Thai text matched against the Fiscal Policy Office release; Colombia's Spanish release sits behind a bot check, so its official English release is cited); sources are shown only once published; no wording names a later year.
note: Where an official objective refers to an index other than headline CPI (the Federal Reserve's PCE price index; see each row), the benchmark is applied to headline CPI. India's benchmark is the RBI's stated CPI objective for the current period. Benchmarks apply to the headline CPI series used here. Each benchmark is the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at the cutoff; China's is the government's annual CPI objective, announced each March (until then the previous year's applies). Where a range was set, its midpoint is used; for the euro area's ‘below but close to 2%’, 1.9%. Sources are listed only if published on or before the edition’s last eligible day.

US.wording: FOMC Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy, 25 Jan 2012: 'The Committee judges that inflation at the rate of 2 percent, as measured by the annual change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures, is most consistent over the longer run with the Federal Reserve's statutory mandate.'
US.index: PCE price index; benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: Federal Reserve press release, FOMC statement of longer-run goals and policy strategy, 25 Jan 2012

XM.wording: 'A year-on-year increase in the HICP for the euro area of below 2%' … 'maintain inflation rates close to 2% over the medium term' (below but close to 2%: 1.9% used).

urls.label: ECB press release, evaluation of the monetary policy strategy, 8 May 2003

JP.wording: 'The "Price Stability Target" under the Framework for the Conduct of Monetary Policy', 22 Jan 2013: 'the Bank sets the "price stability target" at 2 percent in terms of the year-on-year rate of change in the consumer price index (CPI)' (replacing the 1% 'price stability goal' of February 2012); in the joint statement with the Government the Bank will 'aim to achieve this target at the earliest possible time'.

urls.label: Bank of Japan, The "Price Stability Target" under the Framework for the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 22 Jan 2013
Joint Statement of the Government and the Bank of Japan on Overcoming Deflation and Achieving Sustainable Economic Growth, 22 Jan 2013

GB.wording: June Budget 2010: 'the independent Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Bank of England will continue to target 2 per cent inflation, as measured by the 12-month increase in the Consumer Prices Index (CPI)'.

urls.label: HM Treasury, Budget 2010 (June, HC 61), 22 Jun 2010, para 1.27

CA.wording: Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Inflation-Control Target, 24 Oct 2016: 'The target will continue to be defined in terms of the 12-month rate of change in the total CPI. The inflation target will continue to be the 2 per cent mid-point of the 1 to 3 per cent inflation-control range'; the agreement runs for another five-year period from the start of the current year.

urls.label: Bank of Canada, Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Inflation-Control Target, 24 Oct 2016

AU.wording: Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 19 Sep 2016: 'They agree that an appropriate goal is to keep consumer price inflation between 2 and 3 per cent, on average, over time' (midpoint 2.5%; the previous Statement said 'over the cycle').

urls.label: RBA Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, 19 Sep 2016

CH.wording: The SNB 'regards prices as stable when the national consumer price index (CPI) rises by less than 2% per annum' (midpoint of 0–2%: 1.0%).

urls.label: SNB Quarterly Bulletin 4/2007, 'Inflation forecasting as part of the monetary policy concept'

SE.wording: 'The annual change in the consumer price index (CPI) is to be two per cent', tolerance band ±1 percentage point.

urls.label: Riksbank Monetary Policy Report 2007:3, October 2007
Riksbank Monetary Policy Report 2008:1, February 2008

NO.wording: 'Annual consumer price inflation of approximately 2.5% over time.'

urls.label: Norges Bank Monetary Policy Report 3/07

NZ.wording: Policy Targets Agreement signed 20 Sep 2012: 'The agreement continues to require the Reserve Bank to keep CPI inflation between 1 per cent and 3 per cent on average over the medium term. Within this target, the new agreement now requires the Bank to focus on keeping future average inflation near 2 per cent.'

urls.label: Minister of Finance press release, 'New Policy Targets Agreement signed today', 20 Sep 2012 (Scoop)

CN.wording: Report on the Work of the Government delivered 5 Mar 2016, main development targets: 'CPI increase kept at around 3%' (the previous year's objective, which applies until the new annual objective is announced; a government objective, not a PBoC target).

urls.label: Beijing Review, 'Highlights of Chinese Government Work Report for 2016', 5 Mar 2016
Report on the Work of the Government, delivered 5 Mar 2016 (full text, Embassy of China in the US)

IN.wording: RBI Monetary Policy Committee, resolution of 4 Oct 2016: policy is set 'in consonance with the objective of achieving consumer price index (CPI) inflation at 5 per cent by Q4' of the fiscal year ending in March of the current year 'and the medium-term target of 4 per cent within a band of +/- 2 per cent' (the statutory target of 4% with tolerance levels of 2% and 6%, notified 5 Aug 2016). Until that fiscal year ends, the 5 per cent objective is the benchmark for the current period.

urls.label: RBI, Fourth Bi-monthly Monetary Policy Statement 2016–17: Resolution of the Monetary Policy Committee, 4 Oct 2016
Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Finance, 'Central Government in consultation with RBI announces the Inflation Target of Four Percent', 5 Aug 2016

BR.wording: CMN: 'É fixada, para o ano de 2017, a meta para a inflação de 4,5% (quatro inteiros e cinco décimos por cento), com intervalo de tolerância de menos um e meio ponto percentual e de mais um e meio ponto percentual' (4.5% with a ±1.5pp tolerance band).

urls.label: CMN Resolution 4,419 of 25 Jun 2015 (2017 target)

MX.wording: 'Annual CPI inflation of 3 percent' with a variability interval of ±1 percentage point.

urls.label: IMF Public Information Notice 07/140, Mexico Article IV, 13 Dec 2007
Banxico Inflation Report October–December 2007 and Monetary Program for 2008

ZA.wording: Budget Speech, 17 Feb 2010: 'I wish to confirm that the Reserve Bank will continue to pursue a target for CPI inflation of 3 to 6 per cent' (midpoint 4.5%).

urls.label: Minister of Finance, Budget Speech 2010, 17 Feb 2010

TR.wording: End-2017 CPI inflation target of 5%, set jointly with the Government: the CBRT's policy document of 10 Dec 2014 (para 1): 'as in the 2015-2016 period, the inflation target for 2017 is set at 5 percent as per the agreement reached with the government during the preparation of the Medium Term Program (MTP)'; restated in the CBRT's Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy for 2017 (6 Dec 2016), with the uncertainty band 'kept at 2 percentage points in both directions'.

urls.label: CBRT, Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy for 2015, 10 Dec 2014 (para 1)
CBRT, Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy for 2017, 6 Dec 2016

PL.wording: Continuous CPI target of 2.5% with a symmetric ±1 percentage-point band, restated in the Monetary Policy Council's monetary policy guidelines (resolution of 30 Sep 2009, published 14 Oct 2009).

urls.label: Monitor Polski No. 66, item 868: MPC resolution of 30 Sep 2009 on monetary policy guidelines (published 14 Oct 2009)

HU.wording: 'An inflation rate near the 3 per cent medium term objective.'

urls.label: MNB Quarterly Report on Inflation, November 2007
MNB Quarterly Report on Inflation, February 2008

CZ.wording: 'The CNB announces the new inflation target as annual consumer price index growth of 2% (with a tolerance band of ± 1%), effective from January 2010'.

urls.label: CNB press release, 'The CNB's new inflation target and changes in monetary policy communication', 8 Mar 2007
CNB press release, 'The CNB issues Inflation Report I/2010', 12 Feb 2010 (the new inflation target of 2%)

ID.wording: Inflation target for 2017 of 4% with a deviation of 1%, fixed by Finance Minister Regulation 93/PMK.011/2014 (set 21 May 2014, promulgated 3 Jun 2014): '4,0% (empat persen) untuk tahun 2017' … 'dengan deviasi sebesar 1,0% (satu persen)' (annual CPI inflation, year-on-year).

urls.label: Peraturan Menteri Keuangan 93/PMK.011/2014 on the CPI inflation targets, promulgated 3 Jun 2014

KR.wording: Medium-term inflation target set by the Monetary Policy Committee on 16 Dec 2015 for the three years from 2016: 2% in terms of the year-on-year rate of change in the consumer price index ('소비자물가 상승률(전년 동기 대비) 기준 2%'), replacing the 2.5–3.5% range of the previous three years.

urls.label: Pressian (Yonhap), Bank of Korea lowers its medium-term inflation target to 2% (in Korean), 16 Dec 2015
Bank of Korea, financial-market note (in Korean), 17 Dec 2015: markets noting the Bank's new medium-term inflation target of 2%

CL.wording: 'Keep annual CPI inflation around 3% most of the time, within a tolerance range of plus or minus one percentage point.'

urls.label: Central Bank of Chile, Monetary Policy in an Inflation Targeting Framework, January 2007

CO.wording: Board of Directors, 25 Nov 2016: the Board 'confirms that the inflation target is 3.0%, and reiterates that the monetary policy actions undertaken so far are aimed at driving inflation to a range of 3.0% ± 1 pp in 2017 and consolidate its convergence to 3.0%' ('ratifica que la meta de inflación es 3%').

urls.label: Banco de la República, Board of Directors press release, 25 Nov 2016

TH.wording: Monetary-policy target for 2017 approved by the Cabinet on 20 Dec 2016, as agreed between the Monetary Policy Committee and the Minister of Finance: annual average headline inflation of 2.5 ± 1.5 percent as the medium-term monetary-policy target and the target for 2017 ('อัตราเงินเฟ้อทั่วไปเฉลี่ยทั้งปีที่ร้อยละ 2.5 ± 1.5 เป็นเป้าหมายของนโยบายการเงินสำหรับระยะปานกลาง และเป็นเป้าหมายสำหรับปี 2560').

urls.label: Bank of Thailand, MPC announcement on the monetary-policy target for 2017 (in Thai), 21 Dec 2016
Fiscal Policy Office, Ministry of Finance, press release No. 169/2559 (in Thai), 21 Dec 2016

CN.wording: Report on the Work of the Government delivered 5 Mar 2017, main targets for this year: 'CPI increase kept at around 3 percent' ('居民消费价格涨幅3%左右'; a government objective, not a PBoC target; the previous year's was also around 3%).

urls.label: Xinhua, live text of the Report on the Work of the Government (in Chinese), 5 Mar 2017
The State Council, Report on the Work of the Government (full text, as adopted), 16 Mar 2017

IN.wording: RBI Monetary Policy Committee, resolution of 6 Apr 2017 (first of the new fiscal year): policy is set 'in consonance with the objective of achieving the medium-term target for consumer price index (CPI) inflation of 4 per cent within a band of +/- 2 per cent'; the 5 per cent objective for the quarter ending March has reached its horizon, so the statutory 4% target is the benchmark from this statement.

urls.label: RBI, First Bi-monthly Monetary Policy Statement 2017–18: Resolution of the Monetary Policy Committee, 6 Apr 2017

SE.wording: Riksbank, 7 Sep 2017: 'The Executive Board of the Riksbank has decided to adopt inflation measured in terms of the CPIF (the consumer price index with a fixed interest rate) as a formal target variable for monetary policy. The target for monetary policy is that the annual change in the CPIF shall be 2 per cent, that is, the same level previously applied to the CPI'; a variation band of 1–3 per cent replaces the ±1pp tolerance band, applying from the monetary policy decision of 6 Sep 2017.
SE.index: CPIF (CPI with a fixed interest rate); benchmark applied to headline CPI

urls.label: Sveriges Riksbank press release No. 21, 'CPIF target variable for monetary policy', 7 Sep 2017
